newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech party leader charged for inciting hatred - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech party leader charged for inciting hatred - CTK.

text.p: The head of the Czech ultra-right Republican party was detained on Friday and charged with inciting racial hatred for anti-German comments he is accused of making, the CTK news agency said.
He was detained one day after parliament voted to strip him of his immunity over the remarks he was alleged to have made in January during a visit to Prague by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
He was released after being charged, but refused to answer investigators questions, CTK said. Police officials connected to the case were not available for further comment.
The offence is punishable with up to two years in prison.

Sladek has been quoted in local media as telling his followers during a demonstration that "we can only regret that we only killed a few Germans during the war". The remarks have been widely quoted, and never denied.

The Republican party has vehemently opposed a post-World War Two reconciliation agreement with Germany, signed by Kohl and Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus during the German chancellor's visit in January.

Jiri Zajic, secretary of the Republican parliamentary faction in the lower house, told Reuters that Sladek was taken by police in front of the parliament building in central Prague as he arrived for the afternoon session.
"He was taken without any summons or without any official documents," Zajic said.

The Republicans, who won eight percent of the popular vote in last year's lower house elections, see the reconciliation agreement with Germany as a betrayal of Czech interests, and tried in vain to block its approval by parliament earlier this month.

Two other Republican deputies, Josef Krejza and Rudolf Smucr, were also stripped of their immunity on Thursday. They may face charges for disrupting a Czech-German memorial meeting in the former Nazi concentration camp at Terezin in 1994.
